topics.label: Introduction and lecture learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecturer, sets the scope of the cancer lecture series, and outlines the primary learning objectives.

topics.label: Cancer etiology: genetics, environment, and epidemiology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the foundational concepts of cancer development, exploring how endogenous mutations, inherited genetic predispositions, environmental exposures, and stochastic factors interact across populations.

topics.label: Infectious agents and mechanisms of oncogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how viral and bacterial pathogens induce malignancy, examining chronic inflammation, immunosuppression, and chromosomal translocations using Burkitt lymphoma as a primary model.

topics.label: Chemical and physical mutagens and metabolic activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the biochemical mechanisms by which radiation, dietary compounds, and chemical carcinogens cause DNA damage directly or following metabolic activation by host enzymes.

topics.label: Tumor promotion, chronic inflammation, and host susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine non-mutagenic mechanisms of carcinogenesis, demonstrating how chronic inflammation, promotional signaling pathways, and tissue proliferation during specific developmental stages drive tumor progression.

topics.label: Methodologies and considerations for determining carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the genomic, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro experimental approaches used to detect carcinogens and assess exposure risks.

topics.label: Conclusion and lecture summary
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the concluding overview of the lecture's core themes regarding environmental cancer risk and carcinogen potency.
